newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Farm Min still in dark about flood damage.
newsitem.headline: Polish Farm Min still in dark about flood damage.

text.p: Poland's Agriculture Ministry on Monday said no new damage estimates for crops in the flood-hit sourthern and western Poland regions were available yet but new information could appear on Tuesday.

"We have no new information other than what (Agriculture) Minister (Jaroslaw) Kalinowski announced last week...but perhaps on Tuesday new estimates could be avialable," a ministry official told Reuters.

Last week Kalinowski said that roughly 370,000-400,000 hectares of arable land have been flooded and the total cost of lost crops and land recultivation in the flooded regions may reach one billion zlotys.
"These 370,000 hectares include high quality lands ideal for grain or beet crops," the official said, but gave no details.
The agriculture ministry has said that estimating losses was difficult because many areas remain under water and neccessary field work was impossible to carry out.
Kalinowski had also said last week that grain losses might amount to 600,000 to 800,000 tonnes, but stressed the output reduction should not destabilise domestic grains market.
Poland's grain output is expected to come toward the bottom of its estimated range, between 23.6 and 24.7 million tonnes.
In 1996 grain output totalled 24.7 million tonnes and grain reserves are estimated at around four million tonnes. 1997 grains demand is seen at 26.2 million tonnes.
